qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Correct order of bond Angle is:-<\/div>\n"

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Correct order of bond Angle is:-<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"

Explanation:

  • Bond angle is influenced by electron pair repulsion (VSEPR theory), electronegativity of surrounding atoms, and the presence of lone pairs.

Concept:

  1. BF₃ < BCl₃ < BBr₃ (Incorrect): All are sp² hybridized with no lone pairs, resulting in a trigonal planar geometry with ideal bond angle of 120°. The slight increase in bond angle down the group is due to decreasing electronegativity of the halogen, reducing bond pair-bond pair repulsion. 

Correct order: BF₃ ≈ BCl₃ ≈ BBr₃.

  1. SO₂ > SO₃ (Incorrect):

    • SO₂: sp² hybridized with one lone pair, bent shape. Lone pair-bond pair repulsion reduces the bond angle from the ideal 120° to around 119°.

    • SO₃: sp² hybridized with no lone pairs, trigonal planar shape with bond angle of 120°. 

    • Correct order: SO₃ > SO₂.

  2. NO₂ < NO₂⁻ (incorrect):

    • NO₂: Odd electron molecule, bent shape, bond angle around 134°.

    • NO₂⁻: sp² hybridized with one lone pair, bent shape. Lone pair-bond pair repulsion reduces the bond angle to around 115°. 

    • Correct order: NO₂⁻ < NO₂ .

  3. NH₃ > PH₃ (Correct):

    • NH₃: sp³ hybridized with one lone pair, pyramidal shape. Lone pair-bond pair repulsion reduces the bond angle from the ideal 109.5° to around 107°.

    • PH₃: Due to the larger size and lower electronegativity of P, the bond pairs are further from the central atom, leading to less repulsion and a bond angle closer to 90° (around 93.5°). 

    • Correct order: NH₃ > PH₃.

Answer option 4, (NH₃ > PH₃)."

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which among the following is diamagnetic molecule and follow octet rule–<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"Explanation 
1. Diamagnetic vs. Paramagnetic: 
  • Diamagnetic molecules have all electrons paired. 
  • Paramagnetic molecules have unpaired electrons. 
2. Octet Rule: 
  • Atoms achieve a stable electronic configuration by having 8 electrons in their valence shell. Molecules that strictly follow the octet rule do not have any expanded or incomplete octets. 
Concept 
1. NO2 (Nitrogen Dioxide): 
  • Molecular structure: N is bonded to two O atoms with a bent geometry. 
  • Nitrogen has one unpaired electron (odd-electron molecule). 
  • It is paramagnetic and does not strictly follow the octet rule because of the unpaired electron. 
  • NOT the answer. 
2. CLO2 (Chlorine Dioxide): 
  • Molecular structure: Cl is bonded to two O atoms with a bent geometry. 
  • Chlorine has one unpaired electron (odd-electron molecule). 
  • It is paramagnetic and does not strictly follow the octet rule because of the unpaired electron. 
  • NOT the answer. 
3. CO2 (Carbon Dioxide):
  • Molecular structure: Linear geometry with double bonds between carbon and two oxygen atoms. 
  • Carbon and oxygen atoms have all electrons paired. 
  • It is diamagnetic and strictly follows the octet rule (carbon has 4 bonds, and each oxygen has 8 valence electrons). 
  • CORRECT ANSWER. 
4. NO (Nitric Oxide): 
  • Molecular structure: Linear geometry with a single bond between N and O. 
  • Nitrogen has one unpaired electron (odd-electron molecule). 
  • It is paramagnetic and does not strictly follow the octet rule because of the unpaired electron. 
  • NOT the answer. 
Answer option 3"

text_solutions.text:
